By preventing the reabsorption of these neurotransmitters into the presynaptic neuron, the molecule induces a profound accumulation of dopamine in the nucleus accumbens. In cases of acute toxicity or overdose, the physiological consequences can be catastrophic. One may observe cardiac arrhythmias, myocardial infarction due to coronary artery vasoconstriction, or hyperthermia. 

In a post-mortem examination, the presence of cocaine or its metabolites, such as benzoylecgonine, is identified through gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). The concentration levels found in the vitreous humor or femoral blood are critical for determining whether the substance contributed to the cause of death, particularly in instances of sudden cardiac arrest or respiratory depression.
